arch-session-catalog-public-bypasses-ops.action: Make Session::catalog read-only to frontends (pub(crate) field plus a &Catalog accessor) and route non-user bookkeeping through an engine API such as apply_system/commit so the documented ops-only invariant is enforced by visibility, not convention.

arch-export-location-policy-two-authorit.action: Have export_metadata take the resolved removes_location(photo, catalog, o) result (or call it) instead of reading o.remove_location, so one function owns the location decision for all export formats.

findingMessages.arch-session-catalog-public-bypasses-ops: lib.rs:7 documents the Catalog as 'mutated only by ops, so every change is undoable and journaled', but Session exposes it as a public mutable field. A frontend already bypasses it: desktop-host controller.rs:73 calls session.catalog.apply(Op::RemovePhoto) directly when --demo-count trims an opened library. That removal is not pushed to pending_log, not on the undo stack and skips apply_catalog's media.forget, so the in-memory catalog and the library's op log diverge (the photos come back on reopen, or a later snapshot/compaction persists the removal with no undo step).
findingMessages.arch-export-location-policy-two-authorit: removes_location() is the declared seam for location policy ('photo and catalog let library-level privacy rules add to the export option') and the Original/DNG path (prepare_guarded, export.rs:1753-1755) goes through it, but export_metadata() for every rendered format reads o.remove_location directly (export.rs:1597, 1610). The moment a library-level rule is added to removes_location as its doc invites, Original/DNG exports drop GPS while JPEG/TIFF/PSD/WebP/AVIF/JXL exports still embed GPS and place names, leaking the location the rule was meant to strip.
